title: Three levels within thought: imagination, the words in the head, and the real thought
overview:
Chapter 41 opens with the mother who lends her clothing to her daughter, the five *gevuros* of *Ima* that are the combinations of the letters of thought, and the voice of the Torah heard all the way down in speech. Before explaining it, it sets out three levels within thought itself.

The lowest, *maaseh sheb'machshava*, begins with a child, who has pictures but no symbolic thought, and in an adult is thinking how to do, paint or write something; even so, imagination thought actively is higher than dreams. *Dibur sheb'machshava* is another's words registering in the mind like a tape recorder, and thinking how to say what is already thought out. The highest, a person's own thought, has two levels: humming *Adon Olam* without thinking what it means, really the highest *dibur sheb'machshava*, like the telepathy of angels; and the real thought, the *inyan*, which at once brings the letters that fit it. That power to think anything in various combinations depends on *daas*: a child's small *daas* gives small thought, and thought is only as deep as the concept. Thinking about football cannot be very deep.

terms.gloss: thought within thought: a person's own thought; its real level is thinking the inyan itself, the power to think anything in various combinations
speech within thought: another's words registering in the mind, thinking how to say something, or words said in one's head without thinking their meaning
action within thought: thinking of a particular thing, how to do, paint or write it; the beginning of thought
thought within speech: what one thought how to say, as it becomes the thought of the speech
the power of imagination; a picture without letters, all a small child has
imagination; a child's, thought actively, is higher than that of dreams
combinations of letters; the ones that come up in the mind fit exactly the inyan being thought
the mother, who lends her clothing to her daughter
knowledge, being connected to the inyan; the depth and breadth of thought depend on it

sections.title: The mother lends her garments: the letters of thought
sections.summary: The chapter opens with the saying that the mother lends her clothing to her daughter, the five *gevuros* of *Ima* that are the combinations of the letters of thought; the voice of the Torah is heard all the way down, in speech.

phrases.he: (מא) והנה ידוע בענין המאמר דאימא אוזיפת מאנהא לברתא כו'
phrases.en: It's a known thing about what it says: the mother lends her clothing to her daughter.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דאימא כו' פתוחי חותם
חותם שהוא בחינת צרופי התחלקות אותיות דמחשבה,
וכמו שכתוב בזהר על פסוק וקול התור
נשמע בארצנו כו'
phrases.en: is heard in *Malchus*, in the *dibur* (speech)

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: The mother lends her clothing to her daughter: the five *gevuros* (powers of restraint) of *MNTzPCh* of *Ima* (the mother), the combinations of the letters of thought.

*Tor*, in "the voice of the *tor* is heard in our land" (*Zohar*), is a male pigeon and also the giver of the Torah. **Is heard in *Malchus*, in the *dibur***: the voice of the *Aibershter* is heard even in spoken Torah, so Torah has to be said, not just thought.

sections.title: Three levels within thought, beginning with a child's imagination
sections.summary: Thought itself has three levels: thought, speech and action within thought. The lowest, *maaseh sheb'machshava*, begins where a child, who has only pictures, starts to think of a particular thing; in an adult it is thinking how to do, paint or write something.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים שיש ג' מדריגות במחשבה עצמה, והוא בחינת מחשבה דמחשבה ודבור שבמחשבה ומעשה שבמחשבה וביאור הדברים ידוע, להיות מבואר למעלה (באות הל"ז) שיש ג' מדריגות במחשבה ציור בלא אותיות כו', והוא כמו תינוק קטן שאין לו מחשבה בצירופי אותיות עדיין, רק דמיון וציור שבמחשבה שנמשך מכח המדמה בלבד
הגם שנמצא גם בדמיון זה התחלקות חלקים, לצייר בצמצום בדבר מיוחד,
phrases.en: There is some kind of letters, because it's *mechalek* (divides) it into various things, in order to make that *tziyur* (picture).

phrases.he: אבל אינו רק בדמיון, ואינו נקרא מחשבה עדיין שיחשוב באותו דבר, אשר לזה אמרו דקטן אין לו מחשבה כלל וגם כשיגדל מעט ויש לו צירופי התחלקות אותיות במחשבה, אינם אותיות גמורים, רק שיוכל לחשוב בצמצום בדבר הפרטי דוקא כמו לחשוב במוחו בדבר מה שנותנים לו, ויבחין בינו לדבר מה זולתו, עד שיחפוץ בזה וימאס בזה כידוע והוא התחלת ענין המחשבה, ונקרא מעשה שבמחשבה

blocks.text: Thought has three levels: *machshava sheb'machshava* (thought within thought), *dibur sheb'machshava* (speech within thought) and *maaseh sheb'machshava* (action within thought). A small child has only a picture from the *koach hamedame* (power of imagination), divided into parts, some kind of letters, but not yet thought. Grown a little, he thinks of a particular thing, wants it or rejects it: *maaseh sheb'machshava*.

phrases.he: ובגדול היינו מה שחושב איך לעשות דבר ולצייר ולכתוב דרך פרט דוקא,
phrases.en: That's when he's thinking how to do something, or how to paint, or how to write something down.

phrases.he: או שעולה במחשבתו כל מה שצריך לעשות בפועל ממש
וגם מה שמצייר אותיות הכתב במחשבה, או כל דבר גשם נבדל כפרי ועץ, וציור כל תמונה וכהאי גוונא, הכל נקרא עשיה שבמחשבה
ובקטן אין לו גם בחינת מחשבה זו, רק בחינת דמיון לבד

blocks.text: In an adult it is **thinking how to do something, or how to paint, or how to write something down**, or picturing a particular thing, a fruit or a tree. A small child lacks even this: he can picture a tree but cannot think it in words. He has no symbolic thought.

sections.title: Imagination is higher than dreams
sections.summary: Even a child's imagination, thought actively, is higher than the imagination of dreams, which is all that is left in sleep; prophecy and exile are likened to it.

phrases.he: (ועם כל זה הוא למעלה מדמיון החלומות כו')
phrases.en: But nonetheless, this *dimyon* (imagination) that a kid has is higher than the *dimyon* of dreams.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ביד הנביאים אדמה, בכח המדמה שבמחשבה בלבד
לפי שבשעת השינה לא נשאר רק חלק האחרון יותר, שהוא רק הדמיון שבמחשבה (וזהו ענין הגלות שנמשל לשינה, כמו שכתוב היינו כחולמים כו', אך הן מעין הרהורי ליבא כו' כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: Still, a child's *dimyon* (imagination) is higher than dreams: actively picturing is higher than dreaming. Prophecy ("by the hand of the prophets I am imagined") is in imagination, all of thought that is left in sleep; exile is likened to sleep, "we were like dreamers." All this is *maaseh sheb'machshava*.

sections.title: Speech within thought: hearing another's words, and thinking how to speak
sections.summary: *Dibur sheb'machshava* is the words of another's speech registering in the mind, lower than the words a person thinks to himself, and thinking how to say what is already thought out, which becomes the thought within the speech.

phrases.he: ובחינת דבור שבמחשבה הוא כמו שחושב צירופי אותיות הדבור שמדבר זולתו
שזהו למטה מאותיות המחשבה שחושב לעצמו
phrases.en: This is lower than when he's thinking for himself.

phrases.he: בלא שמיעת דבור זולתו

blocks.text: *Dibur sheb'machshava* is like thinking the letters of another's speech: the sound goes from your ear to your brain, and you think the words before you can bring them to an *iyun* (close analysis).
That is lower than thinking for oneself, which here means thinking just the words, not the *sechel* (intellect).

phrases.he: כמו כאשר חושב צירופי אותיות אדון עולם, הרי באופן צירוף מיוחד כזה עצמו,
כאשר שומע במחשבתו דבור זולתו כשמדבר אדון עולם,
phrases.en: When somebody else is talking,

phrases.he: אין זה רק שנחקק אותיות הדיבור זולתו במחשבתו,
phrases.en: as he's talking, the words of his speech become engraved in your mind.

phrases.he: שהוא למטה מאותיות אדון עולם שבמחשבת עצמו
phrases.en: This is a lower thing than something that's already in your mind and you're thinking it.

blocks.title: Humming *Adon Olam*
blocks.text: Like a man walking down the street humming "*Adon Olam asher malach*": he thinks the words, not the *inyanim* (concepts).

Hearing someone else say *Adon Olam*, **the words of his speech become engraved in your mind**, the way a tape recorder records. That is lower than words already in your mind that you think, not as *sechel* but as talking in your own head.

phrases.he: וכך כל מחשבה שחושב איך לדבר
phrases.en: And the same thing when he's thinking how to talk

phrases.he: טרם שמדבר ומיד מדבר נקרא דבור שבמחשבה
וכידוע שזהו מבחינת דבור שבמחשבה נעשה בחינת מחשבה שבדבור
כי ממה שחושב איך לדבר, נעשה אופן המחשבה
phrases.en: From this, what he thinks how to talk, that becomes the thought of the speech

phrases.he: בעת שמתחיל לדבר, מה שרצה במחשבה לדבר כו'
phrases.en: when he starts to talk, what he wanted in thought to say

blocks.text: Thinking how to say something already thought out, just before or while speaking, is also *dibur sheb'machshava*. It becomes *machshava sheb'dibur* (thought within speech): **what he wanted in thought to say** is the thought of the speech as he talks.

sections.title: Thought within thought, and the letters that come with it
sections.summary: The third level, a person's own thought, has two levels: the words said in his head without thinking their meaning, which is really the highest *dibur sheb'machshava*, like the speech of angels; and the real thought, the *inyan*, which brings its letters with it at once.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן המדריגה הג', שהוא מחשבה שבמחשבה, היינו מחשבת עצמו
כשחושב צירופי אותיות אדון עולם בלא דבור או כשחושב שאר ענין דבר מה בצירופים שונים שנקרא אותיות המחשבה
אך גם בזה יש ב' מדריגות,
phrases.en: But this has two levels.

phrases.he: הא' אשר גם הוא בכלל דבור שבמחשבה
phrases.en: The first level is really not *machshava sheb'machshava*; it's really the highest level of *dibur sheb'machshava*.

blocks.text: The third level, *machshava sheb'machshava*, is a person's own thought, *Adon Olam* without speech. But it has two levels, and **the first level is really not *machshava sheb'machshava*; it's really the highest level of *dibur sheb'machshava***.

phrases.he: והוא כאשר אינו חושב כלל את ההשכלה והכוונה שבאותיות אדון עולם וכהאי גוונא,
שהוא ענין מחשבת הממשלה והאדנות,
phrases.en: *Adon Olam*, that means he's thinking how the *Aibershter* is the master of the world.

phrases.he: ואין לו מחשבה כלל בזה, רק צירופי האותיות דאל"ף דלי"ת שבאדון וכהאי גוונא
הגם שהוא בלא דבור, שהוא למעלה משמיעת דבור אדון עולם כנזכר לעיל, מכל מקום נקרא גם זה בשם דבור שבמחשבה

blocks.text: In the first he thinks only the letters, *alef dalet* of *Adon*, not that the *Aibershter* is master of the world. Though above hearing it from another, it is still *dibur sheb'machshava*.
He is humming the song to himself. He knows what it means, but he is not thinking about it, only saying the words inside his head.

phrases.he: (וכענין וקרא זה אל זה, כמו באותיות המחשבה שלנו,
שהיה יכול אדם לקרוא לזולתו בשמו במחשבה מה שקוראו בדבור,
phrases.en: If a person would be able to talk to somebody mentally,

phrases.he: כך הוא בחינת דבור של המלאכים
phrases.en: That's *dibur sheb'machshava*, except by the angels they can do that.

phrases.he: וכן ב' רוחות מספרות זה עם
זה, שאינו נשמע לאדם
phrases.en: a person can't hear it, because it's mental, it's not physical

phrases.he: כו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.title: Telepathy
blocks.text: So too "one called to the other": telepathy. If a person could think at someone instead of talking and be heard, that would be *dibur sheb'machshava*. Angels and spirits talk this way, and a person cannot hear it, because it is mental, not physical.

phrases.he: והב' הוא המחשבה האמיתית
phrases.en: The second one, that's the real thought, not just the letters of thought.

phrases.he: שהוא מה שחושב את ההשכלה של הענין שבאותיות המחשבה,
phrases.en: He's really thinking not the *osios* (letters), but the actual *haskala* (intellectual grasp) of the *inyan* which is inside the *osios hamachshava* (letters of thought).

phrases.he: שמחמתו הוא חושב מיד אופן הצירופים של אותיות הללו
phrases.en: Because of this *inyan*, he immediately thinks the *tzirufim* (combinations) of the letters that go along with it.

phrases.he: (כמו שאנו רואים בצירופי אותיות המחשבה, שמתהווים רק כפי הכוונה שבשכל,
phrases.en: We see that the words that come up in your mind are exactly according to the *inyan* that you're thinking about.

phrases.he: אם כך וכך יתהווה אופן הצירוף כך וכך וכידוע)
phrases.en: When he's thinking about a particular *inyan*, automatically particular letters that describe this *inyan* come up in his head.

blocks.text: The first is a high level of *dibur sheb'machshava*, the interface between the two. **The second one, that's the real thought**.

Here he thinks the *haskala* (intellectual grasp) of the *inyan* inside the letters, and the fitting *tzirufim* (combinations) come up at once, exactly according to the *inyan*. The thinking of the *inyan* is *machshava sheb'machshava*; the letters that come up automatically are the highest level of *dibur sheb'machshava*.

blocks.question: He first called thinking *Adon Olam* *dibur sheb'machshava*; why does he now call it *machshava sheb'machshava* that is really *dibur sheb'machshava*?
blocks.text: The first is where he is not thinking of the *inyan* at all, like doing a rap in his head: he understands the song but only repeats its words. "Tea for two and two for tea": he is not thinking about tea, though he knows that is what it means.

The other means he really thinks an actual *inyan*, the *pnimiyus* (inner part), which at once dresses itself in words of thought. The words are so bound to it they seem to be *machshava sheb'machshava*, but they are its *dibur sheb'machshava*.

sections.title: The power of thought depends on daas: the child and the depth of the concept
sections.summary: The real thought is the power to think anything in various combinations, the vessel of analytical thought, and it depends on *daas*: a child's small *daas* gives him only pictures, and the deeper the concept a person grasps, the deeper his thought.

phrases.he: כמו אם כוונתו בשכל בענין דבר פרט לאיזה מסחור או בענין אדנות, יחשוב בצירופים שונים כפי המכוון דוקא
phrases.en: If he has something in his *sechel* on a certain *inyan*, like in some kind of business, or the *Adnus* (lordship) of the *Aibershter*, he automatically will think it in *tzirufim* of certain letters according to the *mechuvan* (intent) *davka*.

phrases.he: וזהו הנקרא מחשבה שבמחשבה,
שהוא הנקרא כח המחשבה לחשוב כל ענין דבר מה בצירופים שונים
phrases.en: That is called the power of the *machshava* to think anything at all in various *tzirufim*.

phrases.he: (כמו כח הדבור לדבר כל מה שירצה כו' כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: The same like the power of speech to talk whatever he wants to talk.

blocks.text: With an *inyan* in his *sechel*, some business or the *Adnus* (lordship) of the *Aibershter* as in *Adon Olam*, a person thinks it in the *tzirufim* that fit his intent: *machshava sheb'machshava*, the power to think anything in various *tzirufim*, as speech can say anything.

phrases.he: והיא בחינת הכלי למחשבה עיונית
phrases.en: This is the actual *kli* (vessel) of the *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought),

phrases.he: הנקרא מחשבת השכל עצמו
phrases.en: that's called the *machshava* of *sechel* itself.

phrases.he: (הנזכר לעיל באות מ׳) בחינת מלכות דתבונה כו'
והוא המחשבה שתלויה בדעת דוקא
phrases.en: This *machshava* depends on the knowledge *davka*.

blocks.text: This is the *kli* (vessel) of *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought), here called the thought of the *sechel* itself, since even this thought within thought is really letters: *Malchus* of *Tevuna*, already part of the *sechel*.
A person has to be connected to the *inyan* and know what he is thinking.

phrases.he: ולזה אמרו דקטן אין לו מחשבה, דלפי קטנות דעתו כך הוא קטנות המחשבה בלא צירופים כלל,
אבל גדלות הדעת הוא המביא למחשבה בריבוי צירופים שונים
phrases.en: The more a person knows and his *daas* grows, the more his *machshava* can go in *tzirufim meshunim* (various combinations).

phrases.he: ולפי אופן העמקת הדעת בעומק המושג
phrases.en: According to how much he can concentrate deeply into the *omek hamusag* (depth of the concept),

phrases.he: כך יהיה עומק המחשבה
phrases.en: that's how deep his *machshava* will be,

phrases.he: בבחינת עומק מחשבה עיונית הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: in the way of the *omek* of the *machshava iyunis*.

phrases.he: וכמו מה מאד עמקו מחשבותיך,
phrases.en: Like we say to the *Aibershter*, how deep Your thoughts were,

phrases.he: שתלוי בערך עומק המושג דבינה כו'
phrases.en: it has to do according to the depth of the *musag*.

phrases.he: ודי למבין

blocks.text: So a child has no thought: his *daas* (knowledge; the mind's bond with what it understands) is small, barely connected to the little he knows, so he thinks only in pictures and cannot talk. As *daas* grows, thought goes into *tzirufim meshunim* (various combinations).

As deep as he concentrates into the *omek hamusag* (depth of the concept), so deep is his thought; "how very deep are Your thoughts" goes by the depth of the concept of *Bina*. Thinking about football, how deep can it be? The thought is deep because the *musag* is.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the voice of the *tor* heard "in our land", and why does a person have to say the Torah rather than only think it?
What does a small child have in place of thought, and what is the first thought he gains as he grows?
Why is hearing someone else say *Adon Olam* lower than humming it to yourself?
How does thinking how to say something become *machshava sheb'dibur*?
What are the two levels of a person's own thought, and why are the letters that come with the real thought still *dibur sheb'machshava*?
Why does a child have no thought, and what makes a person's thought deep?

notes.text: He reads lines 3-9 and 23-24 with almost no comment (one remark on line 6); their blocks follow the line text as he reads it.

Line 4 refers to chapter 37 ('above, in chapter 37'); he reads it as 'באות ל"ז'. Line 36 refers to chapter 40; the block says chapter 40 from the text's reference, which he reads as 'עיין עליו באות מ'.

The question block (w1496-1679) is his own: he contrasts line 19 (thinking Adon Olam as lower speech-in-thought) with lines 24-27, and answers that the first level of line 25 is not thinking the inyan at all, and 'the other one' (line 30-32) is the real inyan, whose letters are still dibur sheb'machshava. His wording of what was said where is loose ('then later he said he thinks Adon Olam is machshava sheb'machshava, but really it's dibur sheb'machshava'); the block follows it.

Line 2's phrase 'is heard in Malchus, in the dibur' cites only his gloss of 'נשמע בארצנו'; his explanation of tor as 'a male for Torah', with 'the giver is male and Torah is the receiver' then 'tor means the giver of the Torah', is unclear in the transcript; the block keeps only 'the giver of the Torah'.
Line 11 and line 12 have no English phrase: he rephrases line 11 mostly in Hebrew ('like a pri v'etz') and explains line 12 (no symbolic thought) rather than translating it; both are in the block.
Lines 14-16 (prophets, sleep, exile) are read without comment; the block only reports what the text says.
